summary: Okanogan County DNR lookout: fire camp 1914, CCC L-4 cab 1934, present tower 1980, staffed to 2020; the state toppled it in late 2024.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden tower with 14 by 14 foot flattop live-in cab with catwalk (DNR, 1980); the L-4 cab was the 1934 CCC cab
facts.status_note: Removed in late 2024 by the State of Washington, which toppled it with a bulldozer; the FFLA report says a tower with cameras was planned to replace it

access.note: Summit is on DNR land; an alternate route is fully on public lands. The access road crosses private property under a DNR easement, and sources say access has been controversial

visit.trail_note: Alternate route from Sinlahekin Road: about 5.5 miles on a road to the north side of the summit, then ridge game trails (TrailChick lists 12.5 miles round trip)

corrections.why: 6.1 m is 20 ft, the height of the 1934 pole tower. The present 1980 DNR tower is 40 ft per the NHLR and 42 ft per firelookout.com.

corrections.proposed: 40-foot wooden tower with flattop live-in cab with catwalk (DNR, 1980); the L-4 cab was the 1934 CCC cab
corrections.why: The NHLR describes the present structure as a flattop live-in cab with catwalk built in 1980. L-4 is the 1934 CCC cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 5,099 ft (1,554 m). TrailChick and firelookout.com give 5,167 ft; WillhiteWeb gives 5,172 ft. The record keeps the NHLR value (1554.2 m).
TrailChick gives November 2024 and firelookout.com gives October 2024. The FFLA report says late 2024. The story gives both.
NHLR says 40 ft; firelookout.com and TrailChick say 42 ft. The story gives the NHLR figure and says the other source gives 42 feet.
TrailChick says the cab was raised in 1958, and firelookout.com says a 40-foot DNR tower with live-in cab went up in 1958. Left out of the story because the sources disagree on what changed.

sources.title: Report from FFLA Washington Chapter for 2024/2025

notes_for_editor: Fate is corroborated by the FFLA report, TrailChick and firelookout.com. The FFLA report describes the state's plan to replace it with a camera tower. Whether that tower was built is not verified, and the story says only that the state decided to replace it. No remains or view described by any source. Staffing names beyond Knosher and Kresek sit in firelookout.com's list, which is not used. WebSearch budget was used up before this lookout, so no further searches were run.
